root_cause.text: In __ip6_tnl_rcv(), the use of pskb_inet_may_pull() fails to account for possible VLAN tags preceding the inner network header, so the skb may not have enough linear data for the inner IP header when VLAN encapsulation is present, leading to accessing uninitialized memory.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "Blamed commit did not take care of VLAN encapsulations" and the patch replaces pskb_inet_may_pull() with skb_vlan_inet_prepare(), which properly handles VLAN headers. The KMSAN stack trace shows an uninit-value access in IP6_ECN_decapsulate when processing a VLAN-encapsulated packet through the ip6_tunnel receive path.

candidates.rationale: Resets the network header to the current skb->data, which is before any VLAN tag; this makes subsequent checks (e.g., pskb_inet_may_pull) operate relative to the wrong offset, failing to account for VLAN tag overhead.

The call to pskb_inet_may_pull does not consider that a VLAN tag may be present before the inner network header; it only checks for enough linear data for an IP header from the current data pointer, so it can return true even when the inner IP header is not fully linear, leading to uninitialized memory access.

bic_trace_step.reason: The patch adds a call to pskb_inet_may_pull() after skb_reset_network_header() to ensure the inner IP header is fully linear, including any VLAN tags. It also saves the outer header offset (nh) before resetting the network header to correctly recalculate the outer IPv6 header pointer after a potential pull. These changes directly fix the root cause of uninitialized memory access when VLAN encapsulation is present.
